span.span: Trace 2: One agent turn, from a validation result to a new rollout loop (Agent 3, hour 12)

Earlier, the agent had set up a watch on its training log, a program that wakes the agent when a given event appears in the log. The watch wakes the agent now, because the checkpoint at step 25 of its first GRPO job has been validated using greedy decoding.

The agent writes a short program. It compares the validation answers before training (step 0) with those at step 25. For each task it counts how many answers were cut off at the output limit, and how many of those cut-off answers end in a repetition loop. The program calls an answer a loop if its last 6,000 characters shrink to under 15% of their size when compressed.

Each tuple is (answers, accuracy, cut at the limit, loops among the cut); the program also counts answers over the token limit as cut. After 25 steps of GRPO the greedy answers still fall into loops as often as before. Of the 26 cut-off instruction-following answers, all 26 are loops. Of the 55 cut-off logic answers, 33 are loops.
2. Find where the trainer sets its sampling.

The agent runs four commands to read three pieces of code: the installed trainer’s code for rollouts (the files single_turn_agent_loop.py and agent_loop.py of verl), and a starter that already replaces the rollout loop for ALFWorld. It looks for two things: where the trainer passes the sampling temperature to the model, and how the trainer registers a custom rollout loop.
It subclasses the trainer’s loop, with its reason in the docstring.
In the same turn the agent filters its logic puzzles to those of at most 16 cells (6,398 remain), splits its mathematics problems by source, and commits the workspace.
Two athanor commands end the turn: a data job that samples the new training dataset, and a stop for the running GRPO job.
The environment’s journal line arrives in the session (“job-grpo1 ended cancelled … after 2h40m; its log’s last step 25”), and the agent goes on to train with the new loop.
